newsitem.title: USA: Cuban-born banker sentenced for fraud in NY.
newsitem.headline: Cuban-born banker sentenced for fraud in NY.

text.p: Cuban-born businessman Orlando Castro Llanes was sentenced Thursday to at least one year, but no more than three years, for defrauding Venezuelan depositors of millions of dollars through a Puerto Rican bank.
Castro Llanes, 71, had faced up to four years in prison when he was found guilty Feb. 19 after a four-month trial in Manhattan Supreme Court.

Justice Edward McLaughlin stayed the sentence until a May 6 hearing to determine restitution that Castro Lllanes will have to pay. He is eligible for parole almost immediately because he has been in jail since his arrest in April last year.
His son and grandson were also found guilty of fraud and grand larceny Feb. 19 and will be sentenced in the coming weeks.
The complicated financial case was tried in New York because prosecutors said money was fraudulently transferred through New York banks. The transactions included two multi-million dollar transfers.
Jurors had to decide on the issue of whether New York had jurisdiction of the case.

The Cuban exile was accused of playing a key role in Venezuela's banking crisis. He left Venezuela in 1994 after prosecutors produced arrest warrants against him and several associates on charges of financial fraud and other crimes.
